Quick honest note first: ByteDance's "Cinema Studio" (the newer cinematic mode inside their Dreamina / Jimeng family) is a text-to-video and image-to-video tool. It generates short clips (usually a few seconds each) from a prompt, or animates a still image you feed it. So the way to make a "launch story" is not one magic prompt - it is a short shot list, where each shot is its own generation, then you stitch them in CapCut with music and text.

The good news: Haven already has a strong visual identity to build on. The DriftSky star field, the constellation-as-people metaphor, "connection without friction." That metaphor basically writes the film for you. Stars are people. Lines between stars are relationships. A searchable memory network is a living sky.

## How to actually use it

1. Feed it your own frame, do not start from scratch. Export a clean still of the DriftSky background (you have `design/og-card.html` and the `/og.png`). Use image-to-video so the tool animates YOUR look instead of inventing a random one. This keeps brand consistency far better than pure text-to-video.
2. Generate shot by shot. Each clip is 3-5 seconds. A 20-30 second launch teaser is about 6-8 shots.
3. Keep camera language explicit. These models respond to film vocabulary: "slow dolly in," "orbital pan," "rack focus," "anamorphic," "shallow depth of field."
4. Lock the palette in every prompt. Repeat the color words each shot ("deep navy-black sky, soft white and pale-blue stars, faint teal glow") or the tool drifts to a different look between clips.
5. Assemble in CapCut. Add the tagline text, one calm ambient track, and end on the logo + inhavens.com + waitlist CTA.

## The story arc I'd tell

A person feels scattered and disconnected -> stars begin to appear -> lines connect them into constellations -> the sky becomes a searchable, living network -> Haven wordmark. Emotional beat: loneliness to belonging.

## Prompt set (image-to-video, one per shot)

Shot 1 - open on emptiness
```
Image-to-video. Slow push-in on a vast deep navy-black night sky, a few
faint isolated stars drifting alone, soft grain, shallow depth of field,
cinematic anamorphic, calm and slightly lonely mood, subtle particle
drift, 4k, no text.
```

Shot 2 - a spark of recognition
```
A single pale-blue star brightens and gently pulses, warm soft glow
blooming outward, other faint stars begin to appear around it, slow
orbital camera drift, dreamy, hopeful, deep navy background, teal
highlights, cinematic, no text.
```

Shot 3 - connection forms
```
Thin luminous lines draw themselves between nearby stars, forming a
delicate constellation, light traveling along the lines like a signal,
elegant and precise, soft bloom, deep navy-black sky, white and pale-blue
stars, faint teal energy, slow reveal, cinematic, no text.
```

Shot 4 - the network comes alive
```
Camera pulls back to reveal hundreds of stars connected into a vast
glowing web of constellations, gentle waves of light rippling across the
network, breathtaking scale, deep space, cohesive teal and white palette,
serene and awe-inspiring, cinematic wide shot, no text.
```

Shot 5 - land on the brand
```
The constellation network slowly resolves and settles into calm drifting
stars, negative space opens in the center for a logo, minimal, premium,
deep navy-black, soft ambient glow, cinematic, no text.
```

Then in CapCut, over Shot 5, fade in the Haven wordmark, then "Your people, always within reach" (or your real tagline), then inhavens.com and the join-the-waitlist line.

Two things that will make or break it: use image-to-video from your real star field so it looks like Haven, and repeat the palette words in every shot so the clips cut together cleanly.

Want me to tailor this? Tell me:
- The final tagline / one-liner you want on screen
- Length and platform (a 9:16 15s Instagram/TikTok cut lands differently than a 16:9 30s hero video)

I can also pull your actual DriftSky colors out of the code so the palette words in the prompts match the app exactly, and write the on-screen text sequence and a music direction to go with it.

content.text:
You remembered right - and better than what I described before. Here's the real picture:

**Higgsfield does one continuous generation, up to 16 seconds** on the paid Creator/Studio plans (8s on Free). So a whole launch teaser can be a single clip, no stitching required. It also gives you the big models under one subscription now (Veo 3.1, Kling 3.0, Wan 2.6, Minimax Hailuo 2.3), and its real superpower is cinematic camera-motion presets and "AI director" control over movement and lighting. For a 15-16s brand teaser that is plenty.

So the workflow flips from "shot list" to "one strong prompt + the right camera preset."

## How to use it for a one-shot Haven teaser

1. Pick a model that holds coherence over 16s and can include audio - **Veo 3.1** is the safest for a clean single-take brand film. Kling 3.0 if you want more stylized motion.
2. Start from your own frame if you can (upload the DriftSky `/og.png` as the first frame) so the look is truly Haven, not generic space stock.
3. Choose a camera-motion preset that matches the arc - something like a slow **dolly-out / pull-back reveal**, which is exactly the emotional beat you want (one star to a whole connected sky).
4. Set 2.39:1 cinematic or 9:16 depending on where it's going.
5. Add the tagline and CTA as a text layer after, or let Veo bake in ambient sound and add text in CapCut.

## The single full-video prompt (one 16s take)

```
Cinematic 16-second single continuous take. Open on a vast deep navy-black
night sky with one faint, lonely pale-blue star drifting in soft grain and
shallow depth of field. The star gently brightens and pulses; more faint
stars fade in around it. Thin luminous teal-white lines draw themselves
between the stars, forming delicate constellations, light traveling along
the lines like signals. Camera slowly pulls back to reveal hundreds of
stars connecting into a vast glowing living network filling the frame.
Gentle waves of light ripple across the web. The motion settles into calm
drifting stars with open negative space in the center. Palette: deep
navy-black, soft white and pale-blue stars, faint teal glow. Mood: lonely
to hopeful to awe. Anamorphic, soft bloom, subtle particle drift, premium
and serene. No text, no people.
```

Camera preset: **slow pull-back / dolly-out.** Mood: calm, cinematic. Then drop your wordmark + tagline + inhavens.com over the last 3-4 seconds in CapCut.

One trade-off to know: a single 16s generation gives you a seamless take but less control over each beat. If a specific moment lands wrong (say the "lines connecting" reads messy), you re-roll the whole clip rather than fixing one shot. For a first launch that's usually fine, and the seamlessness is worth it.
